app.name: AlphaMaster
app.foundationNote: Theme, density and direction are applied to the document root, so every component below inherits them without asking.

signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.identifierRequired: Enter your email address or phone number.
signIn.attemptsRemaining_one: {{count}} attempt remaining before this account is locked.
signIn.attemptsRemaining_other: {{count}} attempts remaining before this account is locked.

mfa.challengeDescription: Enter the code from your authenticator app, or have one sent to you.
mfa.codeHint: Six digits, or one of your recovery codes.
mfa.expiredBody: Start again from the sign-in screen.

enrol.title: Set up two-factor authentication
enrol.description: Administrators cannot sign in without a second factor.
enrol.qrLabel: Scan this code with your authenticator app
enrol.qrFailed: The code could not be drawn. Enter the secret below by hand instead.
enrol.secretLabel: Or enter this secret by hand
enrol.recoveryBody: These are shown once and cannot be retrieved again. Each one can be used a single time to sign in if you lose your second factor.
enrol.acknowledge: I have saved these recovery codes somewhere safe.

verify.title: Verify your email address
verify.description: We need to know the address on this account reaches you.
verify.sent: The link is on its way. Follow it, then continue below.
verify.already: This address is already verified. Continue below.

suspended.title: This account is suspended
suspended.body: Sign-in is blocked while the account is suspended. Someone with administrator access can restore it.

notAdministrator.title: This is the administration console
notAdministrator.body: The account signed in is not an administrator, so there is nothing here for it. Nothing is wrong with the account itself.

cover.statement: The system, and everyone who may change it.
cover.detail: Configuration, integrations, access and the record of every change — behind one perimeter, on one credential.

auth.captchaUnavailable: The verification challenge could not be loaded, so sign-in cannot be completed. An administrator can switch the captcha off in Settings › Auth.
auth.captchaInvisible: This sign-in is protected by reCAPTCHA. No challenge is shown; the check runs in the background.

notFound.title: Nothing lives at this address
notFound.body: No module claims this path. A bookmark or a link may be out of date.

crash.title: The console stopped
crash.body: Something in the interface failed to render. The platform itself is unaffected — nothing was saved or lost by this.

platform.title: Platform
platform.scope: This probe reports that the application is running. It does not check the database or the cache.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.none: No vendor capability is configured or has been used.
integrations.noActiveProvider_one: One provider is configured and none is active.
integrations.noActiveProvider_other: {{count}} providers are configured and none is active.
integrations.noCredentials: The active provider has no credentials, so every attempt will be refused.

attention.title: Needs attention
attention.skipped: Not checked, because this account may not read what it needs: {{checks}}.

finding.capability-failing_one: One capability is failing every attempt.
finding.capability-degraded_one: One capability is failing some attempts.
finding.platform-closed: The platform is closed for maintenance.

why.platform-silent: The liveness probe did not report a healthy application.
why.administrator-blocked: The perimeter refuses an account that is suspended, has an unconfirmed address, or has no confirmed second factor.
why.capability-failing: Every recent attempt through the active provider was refused.
why.capability-degraded: Some recent attempts through the active provider were refused.
why.action-failed: Recorded in the audit trail with a failed outcome.
why.capability-uncredentialed: The active provider holds no credentials, so every attempt will be refused before it is made.
why.platform-closed: Maintenance mode is on, so the API refuses every caller except an administrator whose token bypasses it — which is why nothing else here looks wrong.

state.title: Platform
state.trailNote: Entries retained. The API does not publish a retention window.

next.title: Next actions
next.noneNote: This lists work the console can carry out. Something can need attention and still have no screen here to act on it.

because.administrator-blocked: They are refused at sign-in until the account is active, the address confirmed and a second factor enrolled.
because.capability-failing: Every recent attempt was refused. Integrations shows which provider is answering and what it returned.
because.capability-degraded: Some recent attempts were refused. Integrations shows which provider is answering and what it returned.
because.test-mail: Mail is configured and has never been used, which is the state most easily mistaken for working.
because.capability-uncredentialed: The active provider holds no credentials, so every attempt will be refused before it is made.

settings.chooseGroup: Choose a group to see what it holds.
settings.unknownGroup: No such group. A link or a bookmark may be out of date.
settings.deprecatedNote: Withdrawn from the catalogue. It is still stored and still read, but it is no longer meant to be set.
settings.mailSent: A test message was sent to the address on your account.
settings.malformedJson: That is not valid JSON yet, so it has not been staged.
settings.versionHelp: The version this page was read at. A save carries it, so a change made elsewhere is refused rather than overwritten.
settings.unavailableUntil: Unavailable until {{keys}} is configured. Setting it now would have no effect.

readOnly.permission: Read only. Changing this needs the {{permission}} permission.
readOnly.declared: Read only. The platform does not allow this one to be changed here.

settings.secretExplanation: Stored encrypted and never returned. Replace it by rotating rather than editing.

secret.verifyNote: The platform verifies the candidate before storing it. Nothing is written unless it works.

media.tooLarge: That file is larger than the platform accepts (100 MB).
media.notAnImage: That file is not an image.
media.rejectedTooLarge: The file was refused before it reached the platform, because it is larger than this deployment accepts.

validation.email: That does not look like an email address.
validation.url: That does not look like a URL.
validation.ulid: That is not a valid identifier.

precondition.title: The save carried no version
precondition.body: The platform refused the write because it did not say which version of the group it was built on. Reload the group and try again.

conflict.title: Someone else saved first
conflict.body: This group changed after this page was loaded, so the save was refused rather than overwriting it. Your edits are still here.
conflict.rebase: Load current values, keep my edits

history.title: History
history.none: Nothing in this group has been changed yet.

roles.label: Name
roles.labelHint: What administrators will see. The identifier the platform stores is derived from this once and never changes afterwards.
roles.renameHint: Renaming changes only what is displayed. The identifier below is what permissions and assignments reference, and it does not move.
roles.deleteWarning: The role is removed from every account holding it, and those accounts lose whatever it granted. If it is what grants your own administrative access, you will lose that too. The platform does not refuse this.
roles.readOnly: You may read these permissions but not change them. Creating, changing and deleting a role need the roles.update permission.

access.effectiveNote: Everything this account holds, directly or through a role. The platform does not say which, so neither does this.
access.filterNote_zero: Filtered in the browser. There is nothing to filter yet.
access.filterNote_one: Filtered in the browser across the one account the platform returned.
access.filterNote_other: Filtered in the browser across all {{count}} accounts. The platform returns them in one response.
access.mfaNote: Whether a confirmed second factor exists. Which one is not published.
access.rolesReadOnly: Changing roles needs the roles.update permission.
access.permissionsHidden: Seeing the permission catalogue needs the permissions.view permission.
access.chooseUser: Choose an account to inspect it.
access.unsupported: Deleting an account is not offered: the platform publishes no endpoint for it. Stopping sign-in is the reversible equivalent, and it is above.

users.name: Name
users.emailChangeHint: Changing the address marks it unverified. The account keeps everything it had; the platform simply stops treating the new address as confirmed.
users.phoneHint: Optional. Include the country code — the platform stores E.164 and will not guess one.
users.passwordHint: Set once, here. The account can change it afterwards, and no administrator can set it again from this console.
users.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
users.activeOnCreateNote: Leave it off to create the account now and let it in later.
users.createNote: This creates a regular account. Making it an administrator is a separate, deliberate step, taken from the account panel afterwards.
users.localeHint: The language the platform writes to this account in.
users.noPasswordEdit: There is no password field on an edit. Setting somebody else’s password is a credential reset, and this platform does not offer one from here.
users.deactivateWarning: The account is signed out everywhere at once and refused at sign-in until it is allowed back. Nothing it owns is deleted, and this can be undone.
users.cannotDeactivateSelf: You cannot stop your own account signing in.

permissions.catalogueNote: Every permission the platform enforces is defined in its code and seeded from there. Permissions are not created, renamed or removed — not here and nowhere else in the console. What an operator changes is which roles carry them.
permissions.count_other: {{count}} permissions, grouped by the module that owns each.
permissions.orphanNote: A permission no role carries is enforced by the platform and held by nobody.
permissions.rolesHidden: Seeing which roles carry a permission needs the roles.view permission.
permissions.denied: Reading the permission catalogue needs the permissions.view permission.

access.phoneConfirmNote: Only the account holder can confirm a number, from their own account page. Changing the number here clears the confirmation.

integrations.noProviders: No vendor provider is configured on this deployment.
integrations.noProvidersNote: Providers are shipped with the platform for the capabilities it can consume. There is no way to add one from here, and no endpoint behind such a control if there were.
integrations.unavailable: The provider list could not be read.
integrations.activityUnavailable: The activity log could not be read, so what this provider has actually done is unknown.
integrations.chooseProvider: Choose a provider to inspect or configure it.
integrations.defaultNeedsActive: A provider has to be active before its capability can be pointed at it.
integrations.label: Label
integrations.priorityHint: Lower runs first when the default is unavailable. 0 to 1000.
integrations.settingsHint: Non-secret configuration this driver reads. The platform does not publish which names a driver expects, so they are typed rather than chosen.
integrations.name: Name
integrations.readOnly: You may read this provider but not change it. Changing one needs the integrations.update permission.
integrations.noAttempts: Nothing has been sent through this provider in the recorded window.
integrations.noFailures: No failure is recorded in the window.

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.explanation: Stored encrypted and never returned by the platform, so they cannot be shown here. What is stored can be replaced or removed, not read.
credentials.replaceWarning: What you submit becomes the whole credential set for this provider. Anything stored under a name you do not repeat is removed.
credentials.startEmpty: Add each credential this driver needs.
credentials.clearWarning: This removes every stored credential for this provider. Calls through it will be refused until new ones are supplied.

usage.title: Vendor activity
usage.window_zero: The platform publishes the most recent attempts across every capability. None is recorded.
usage.window_one: The platform publishes the most recent attempts across every capability. {{count}} is recorded, and the filter applies to those.
usage.window_other: The platform publishes the most recent attempts across every capability. {{count}} are recorded, and the filter applies to those.

languages.intro: These are the languages the platform will accept content and translations in. Whether this console can be read in one is a separate matter: the Admin ships its own message catalogues, and a language added here becomes available to the platform without making the interface speak it.
languages.chooseLanguage: Choose a language to inspect or change it, or add one.
languages.makeDefaultActivates: Making a language the default activates it: the platform will not fall back to a language it has been told not to serve.
languages.defaultStaysOn: The default language cannot be switched off. Make another one the default first.
languages.codeHint: The identifier the platform stores against content and translations. Two to ten characters.
languages.codeChangeHint: Changing this changes what settings and notification translations are keyed to. Existing content stays under the old code.
languages.name: Name in English
languages.nativeNameHint: What a reader of this language calls it. Shown to them in the switcher.
languages.orderHint: Lower comes first wherever languages are listed.
languages.noDelete: A language cannot be deleted. Settings and notification translations reference it by code, so the platform deactivates rather than removes.
languages.noInterfaceTranslation: This console ships no message catalogue for {{code}}. The platform will serve the language; the Admin interface will still be read in one it has.

media.chooseFile: Choose a file to inspect it, or upload one.
media.failed: This file did not complete intake
media.removeWarning: The record is removed now and the stored file is purged later by the retention job. Nothing in the platform restores either.
media.removeDenied: You may read this file but not remove it. Removing one needs the media.delete permission.
media.noReplace: A stored file cannot be replaced or renamed. The bytes behind an identifier never change, which is what makes them cacheable forever; upload a new file instead.

empty.title: Nothing is stored yet.
empty.body: Uploading a file here puts it through the platform intake: it is stored, scanned where a scanner exists, and becomes servable once it is ready.
empty.filteredBody: The filter is applied by the platform across everything it holds, not only this page, so this is the whole answer.

preview.not-visual: No inline preview for this type
preview.refused: The platform did not serve this file

upload.title: Upload a file
upload.fileHint: Up to {{size}}. What the file is gets decided from its bytes by the platform, not from its name.
upload.collectionHint: Groups files that belong together. Lower case, starting with a letter.
upload.collectionInvalid: Lower case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
upload.publicNote: A public file is readable by anyone signed in.
upload.privateNote: A private file is readable by whoever uploaded it, and by whatever the owning module allows once it is attached to something.
upload.accepted: The file was accepted and is being processed.
upload.pipelineNote: An accepted file is not immediately servable: it is scanned and processed first, and appears in the library while that happens.

preferences.intro: What the platform tells you, and how it reaches you. These are your own settings about your own messages: there is no endpoint that reads or writes anybody else’s, so this page cannot show you theirs.
preferences.lockedNote: A locked row cannot be switched off. The in-app record is always written — it is the evidence the platform decided to tell you something — and a security alert is not a preference.

templates.intro: What every recipient reads. Editing a template changes the message for everyone the platform sends it to.
templates.choose: Choose a notification to read or change its wording.
templates.inactiveNote: An inactive template is not sent. The notification is still recorded; nothing is worded for it.
templates.readOnly: You may read this wording but not change it. Editing needs the notifications.update permission.
templates.subject: Subject
templates.bodyHint: Placeholders the platform substitutes are written as they appear here; nothing in this field is interpreted by the console.
templates.noWording: Nothing is written for this language yet. The platform falls back to the default language when it sends.
templates.incomplete: A translation needs both a subject and a body. Incomplete: {{languages}}.

inbox.intro: Every notification the platform raised for this account. The in-app record is the one channel that cannot be silenced, because it is the evidence a notification was sent at all — which is also why nothing here deletes one.
inbox.none: The platform has not sent this account anything yet.

announce.intro: The one notification an administrator writes. Everything else the platform sends describes something that happened; this is the case where you are the event.
announce.subject: Subject
announce.bodyHint: Written literally. Nothing in it is treated as a placeholder, so a colon in your text stays a colon.
announce.audienceHint: Suspended accounts receive nothing: the in-app record is where this lands, and an account that cannot sign in cannot read one.
announce.confirm: This goes to {{audience}} and cannot be unsent. Each recipient reads it in their own language, and it lands in their notifications rather than their inbox unless they asked for email.
announce.sent_zero: Nobody matched that audience, so nothing was sent.

audit.intro: Every administrative action the platform recorded, newest first. The trail is append-only: nothing here edits or removes an entry, and the filters below are the ones the platform indexes on, so an answer is drawn from the whole trail rather than from the page in front of you.
audit.choose: Choose an entry to read what was recorded.

empty.title: Nothing matches.
empty.body: The platform answered this filter across the whole trail, not just this page, so this is the complete answer.

filters.subject: Subject
filters.note: These are the platform’s own filters. There is no free-text search: the trail is indexed on these columns, and searching the recorded context would be a scan over the one column whose contents differ for every action.

fields.subject: Subject
fields.noContext: Nothing beyond the fields above was recorded.

archive.warning: This exports and then removes every entry older than the platform’s retention window, which is set in operations settings rather than chosen here. Verification runs before removal: if it fails, nothing is removed. Removed entries are not readable from this console again.
archive.moved_zero: No entry was old enough to archive.
archive.moved_one: One entry was moved out of the active trail.
archive.moved_other: {{count}} entries were moved out of the active trail.

configuration.intro: Moving this deployment’s configuration in and out deliberately. Not a database backup — infrastructure takes those, on its own schedule and with its own retention. This is for seeding an environment, moving configuration between them, and answering what something was set to without restoring a database.

export.title: Export
export.body: Writes a snapshot to the configured disk and answers with a receipt. It never contains decrypted secrets, audit records, second factors, or accounts — those exclusions are structural rather than filtered.
export.includeSecretsNote: A secret travels as the ciphertext already stored, or not at all. Portable within one deployment and worthless outside it — but worth stealing, so it has to be asked for.
export.omitted: Omitted secrets: {{keys}}. A restore elsewhere will need these supplied by hand.

restore.title: Restore
restore.body: Reads an export back over what is running. It validates before it writes and reports what it declined rather than coercing it.
restore.locationHint: A path on the deployment’s own disk, which is where its access controls apply. There is no upload, because the endpoint takes none.
restore.locationInvalid: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and slashes. It cannot climb out of the disk.
restore.warning: This rewrites configuration wholesale from a document you may not have read. It is not reversible from here: settings history covers a group at a time, not a restore of everything at once.
restore.keyMatched: The encryption key matched, so encrypted credentials in the export were restorable.
restore.keyDiffered: The encryption key differs from the one that wrote this export, so every encrypted credential was skipped. Everything else was restored.

history.elsewhere: Configuration history and rollback live in Settings, on the group they belong to, where the version an operator is rolling back to can be previewed against the values it would replace. There is deliberately no second history here: two accounts of the same change would disagree the first time either moved.

account.description: What the platform knows about the account you are signed in as.
account.noPhone: The platform has no phone number for this account.
account.phoneVerifiedNote: Somebody answered a code sent to this number.
account.confirmIntro: Have a code sent to this number, then enter it below. This confirms that the number reaches you.
account.codeHint: The digits in the message. It expires shortly after it is sent.
account.numberSetByAdministrator: The number itself is set by an administrator. Ask one to change it, then confirm the new number here.

translations.description: What the platform says, in every language it says it in. The languages workspace decides which languages exist; this is what is written in them.
translations.readOnly: You can read this content but not change it.
translations.nothingReadable: There is no translatable content you have permission to read.
translations.oneLanguage: The platform serves one language, so there is nothing to translate into.
